lines.text: Texas was its own country for nine years. So why did it ever give that up?
And this was a real country. Its own president. Its own army. Its own currency, and embassies in London and Paris.
It was bigger than France, and it had beaten Mexico in a war to exist at all.
The obvious answer is money. Texas was broke.
A hundred and thirty-five thousand people, and ten million dollars of debt it could never pay.
But that is not why it joined. Because Texas asked to join, and America said no.
Texas allowed slavery. Letting it in would tip the balance of the Senate, and Washington would not touch it.
Britain. Texas started negotiating with London, and Britain wanted exactly what Texas had: cotton, and a country wedged under the United States.
lines.say: Britain. Texas started negotiating with London. And Britain wanted exactly what Texas had. Cotton, and a country wedged under the United States.

lines.text: A British ally on the southern border was the one thing Washington could not allow.
In 1845, the answer became yes. Texas joined, and it joined fast.
lines.say: In eighteen forty-five, the answer became yes. Texas joined, and it joined fast.

lines.text: And here is what nobody expects.
Annexing Texas started a war with Mexico. America won it, and took everything from the Rio Grande to the Pacific.
California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona. Texas is the reason America reaches the west coast at all.
